caption:
This morning: fewer than half of the stats AI assistants quote lead to a study that says the same. I went back in to check.

The page AI cited had the figure 82% of the time. Only 37% of company-blog citations led to a real study. Claude quoted 6.8 numbers per answer, ChatGPT 1.3.

My take: a quoted number is not a source. Trace it, and publish your own primary data so AI can trace it too.

Comment GEO and I will send you the details by DM.

Sources in the first comment.

scenes: This morning: fewer than half of the stats AI assistants quote reach a study that says the same. I went back in to check.
First, the assistants rarely invent numbers. The page they cited contained the figure 82% of the time. The problem is which page.
Second, more than half of first citations were company blogs, and only 37% of those led to a real study.
Third, volume differs a lot. ChatGPT quoted 1.3 numbers per answer, Claude quoted 6.8, so more numbers means more to check.
My take: a quoted number is not a source. Trace it, and publish your own primary data so AI can trace it too.
